data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'naba' which means 'to give the news'. The name Nabiih is given to those who deliver the message of Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the greatest example of a Nabiih in Islamic history. The name Nabiih carries the meaning “Prophet, Messenger” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Nabiih usually hope their child will grow to embody prophet, messenger and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nabiih total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

Thus, the name Nabiih honors the role of the prophets in spreading the message of God and inspiring the faith and obedience of the believers.

historical_references.reference: Nabih ibn al-Harith As-Sabbi, a companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and one of the Ten Promised Heaven. He was born in the tribe of As-Sabaa in Yemen. According to hadiths, he was given the title 'Nabih' meaning 'Prophet' because he resembled the Prophet (pbuh) in manners and speech.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history and Prophet Muhammad's companions

historical_references.reference: Nabih ibn Wahb, a poet from the Banu Tamim tribe in pre-Islamic Arabia. He was known for his poetic skills and was considered one of the greatest poets in pre-Islamic Arabian literature. The title 'Nabih' in his case was a poetic honorific meaning 'wise and eloquent'.
historical_references.context: Pre-Islamic Arabian literature and poetic traditions
